question.text: An offshore Mauritius fund uses an Indian investment adviser to source deals. What is the principal tax risk if this relationship is poorly documented?

answer.text: The offshore fund will lose its SEBI FVCI registration automatically.
The 'Place of Effective Management' (POEM) of the offshore fund may be held to be in India, subjecting its global income to Indian tax.
The Indian adviser will be deemed the GP of the offshore fund.
Mauritius will impose 30% withholding tax on all distributions.

explanation.text: The Logic: If the Indian advisory office's scope is not properly restricted through documentation, Indian tax authorities may hold the offshore fund to have a Permanent Establishment (PE) or its Place of Effective Management (POEM) in India. POEM in India makes the fund a resident for Indian tax purposes, and resident taxation extends to worldwide income. The Trap: FVCI loss has no automatic link to advisory relationships. GP-deeming is fabricated. Mauritius withholding claim is invented. Note: The workbook supports offshore funds using Indian investment advisers, the risk that an Indian advisory office could be construed as PE/POEM, and the need to restrict advisory-office scope through documentation.
